document.title: Memorandum for The President from Zbigniew Brzezinski, "Reflections on Soviet Intervention in Afghanistan"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan, 1979: Not Trump’s Terrorists, Nor Zbig’s Warm Water Ports | National Security Archive
document.note: Brzezinski's analysis set the stage for the forceful U.S. response, including grain embargoes and ramped-up covert support to the Afghan guerrillas. It lays out the "arc of crisis" and Moscow's "age-long dream" of Indian Ocean access. Redactions at declassification concerned Pakistan, including that Pakistan's security policy cannot be dictated by nonproliferation policy. Brzezinski cautions against being sanguine about a Soviet Vietnam.

events.description: Brzezinski sends memorandum to the President on the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan, urging more money, arms and technical advice for the rebels and a policy review toward Pakistan
NSC meeting on Friday to focus on Afghanistan and Iran
Brzezinski sends the President a memorandum reflecting on the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan and recommending support for the resistance.
SCC meeting minutes on Afghanistan and Iran delivered to the President.
NSC meeting planned for Friday focusing on Afghanistan and Iran.
The US assumed the British role of maintaining Afghanistan as a buffer state.
Planned Harold Brown visit to China.

relationships.detail: Brzezinski as National Security Adviser writes memorandum to the President.
relationships.quote: MEMORANDUM FOR: THE PRESIDENT. FROM: ZBIGNIEW BRZEZINSKI

relationships.detail: Memo recommends the US provide more money, arms and technical advice to the rebels (proposed; the direction is the recipient funded by the US).
relationships.quote: This means more money as well as arms shipments to the rebels, and some technical advice

relationships.detail: Memo proposes encouraging Pakistan to help the rebels.
relationships.quote: we must both reassure Pakistan and encourage it to help the rebels

relationships.detail: Memo proposes the Chinese help the rebels.
relationships.quote: We should encourage the Chinese to help the rebels also

relationships.detail: Guerrillas oppose the Soviet intervention.
relationships.quote: Soviet intervention in Afghanistan poses for us an extremely grave challenge

relationships.detail: Brzezinski says he will send the President a proposed agenda for the NSC meeting on Friday, focused on Afghanistan and Iran.
relationships.quote: I will be sending you separately a proposed agenda for the NSC meeting on Friday

relationships.detail: The memorandum is on White House letterhead from Brzezinski to the President.
relationships.quote: THE WHITE HOUSE

relationships.detail: The President receives SCC minutes on Afghanistan and Iran.
relationships.quote: you are receiving today's SCC minutes on both subjects

relationships.detail: The Soviet Union intervened in Afghanistan; Brzezinski assesses the intervention as a grave challenge that could become a Soviet Vietnam.
relationships.quote: the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan poses for us an extremely grave challenge

relationships.detail: Moscow's historic aim is direct access to the Indian Ocean, which would be fulfilled if the Soviets succeed in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: the age-long dream of Moscow to have direct access to the Indian Ocean will have been fulfilled

relationships.detail: The US assumed in 1945 the British role of keeping Afghanistan as a buffer state against Russian expansion.
relationships.quote: the British provided the barrier to that drive and Afghanistan was their buffer state. We assumed that role in 1945

relationships.detail: The Iranian crisis led to a collapse of the balance of power in Southwest Asia.
relationships.quote: the Iranian crisis has led to the collapse of the balance of power in Southwest Asia

relationships.detail: Pakistan is described as internally unstable and externally apprehensive amid regional crisis; Afghanistan is in turmoil.
relationships.quote: Pakistan Is both unstable internally and extremely apprehensive externally

relationships.detail: The Soviet intervention could produce a head-to-head confrontation with the US and threatens SALT.
relationships.quote: it could bring us into a head to head confrontation with the Soviets

relationships.detail: Soviet assertiveness is seen in Cambodia as well as Afghanistan; Soviet-sponsored actions in Cambodia have taken a toll.
relationships.quote: Soviet assertiveness in Afghanistan and in Cambodia is not effectively restrained by the United States

relationships.detail: The Chinese will note that the US does not effectively restrain Soviet assertiveness.
relationships.quote: The Chinese will certainly note that Soviet assertiveness

relationships.detail: About 300,000 Afghan refugees are already in Pakistan.
relationships.quote: There are already 300,000 refugees from Afghanistan in Pakistan

relationships.detail: The guerrillas oppose the Soviet intervention but are described as badly organized and poorly led.
relationships.quote: The guerrillas are badly organized and poorly led

relationships.detail: Brzezinski recommends more money, arms shipments and technical advice to the rebels.
relationships.quote: This means more money as well as arms shipments to the rebels, and some technical advice

relationships.detail: The US should encourage Pakistan to help the rebels, with guarantees and arms aid to Pakistan.
relationships.quote: we must both reassure Pakistan and encourage it to help the rebels

relationships.detail: Brzezinski proposes more guarantees and more arms aid to Pakistan.
relationships.quote: more arantees to it, more arms aid

relationships.detail: Brzezinski recommends encouraging China to help the rebels.
relationships.quote: We should encourage the Chinese to help the rebels also

relationships.detail: The US would coordinate with China on supporting the rebels, and Brown will visit China.
relationships.quote: the substance of the Brown visit to China

relationships.detail: A planned Brown visit to China is mentioned.
relationships.quote: the substance of the Brown visit to China

relationships.detail: US to concert with Islamic countries in propaganda and covert action campaign to help the rebels.
relationships.quote: concert with Islamic countries both in a propaganda campaign and in a covert action campaign to help the rebels

relationships.detail: US should tell the Soviets directly that their actions jeopardize SALT and US-Soviet relations.
relationships.quote: We should inform the Soviets that their actions are placing SALT in jeopardy

relationships.detail: US should consider taking Soviet actions in Afghanistan to the UN as a threat to peace.
relationships.quote: we should consider taking Soviet actions in Afghanistan to the UN as a threat to peace

relationships.detail: China and the Soviet Union supplied arms to North Vietnam; Soviet action in Afghanistan is near the Chinese border.
relationships.quote: Soviet assertiveness so close to their border

sources_cited: SCC minutes on Afghanistan and Iran (26 December 1979)
key_claims: Brzezinski argues that a Soviet success in Afghanistan would fulfil Moscow's age-old dream of direct access to the Indian Ocean.

He warns the intervention could become a Soviet Vietnam but cautions against being too sanguine because the guerrillas are badly organized, poorly led and lack sanctuary, an army or a central government.
He recommends more money, arms shipments and technical advice to the Afghan rebels.
He urges reassuring Pakistan and encouraging it to help the rebels, including more guarantees and arms aid.
He proposes encouraging China to help and coordinating with Islamic countries on propaganda and covert action.
He notes 300,000 Afghan refugees already in Pakistan and says the US could indict the Soviets for causing human suffering.
